step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Inventory: the whiteboard shows S3, CloudFormation, EC2 (three AZ groups under an Auto Scaling group), Direct Connect, the on-prem Techwood/CNN Center site (UserCompanyDataStream) and the satellite uplinks (UserCompanyEdge). 2) Fusion: the three EC2 icons act as one logical playout tier (10 channels per AZ, primary and backup, auto scaling), so they are a single node. The Evertz software (Mediator, ORT, Playtime, CloudBridge) is hosted on EC2 and is recorded in notes rather than as separate nodes, since it is not drawn. 3) Pruning: CloudFormation was only used to deploy the system (about 40 YAML templates) and is not a runtime participant, so it is omitted; it has no ledger connections. 4) Main flow (flow 0): master files QC'd in Atlanta are sent via Aspera to S3, transferred to EC2 running Evertz ORT, played out over Direct Connect back to prem as a unicast signal, then compressed and sent to the uplink for distribution to affiliates (the 'X chain', a tertiary path to air). 5) BCP flow (flow 1): the transcript explicitly states that playout goes via Direct Connect to Hudson Yards (NYC), 8 channels, and is fed to an uplink; the board shows this as a 'BCP' arrow from Direct Connect to the NYC dish, so one extra edge DirectConnect -> UserCompanyEdge is added outside the ledger. 6) Self-check: visual_connections has 5 entries; 6 edges are emitted (5 ledger edges plus 1 explicitly stated BCP edge).

graph.name: WarnerMedia HBO: Cloud Linear Playout
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, Linear Playout, Business Continuity, Hybrid Connectivity
graph.notes: Cloud linear playout for HBO/WarnerMedia in AWS us-east-1 supporting 30 channels. It started as a BCP (business continuity) solution. Deployed through about 40 scrubbed CloudFormation YAML templates as a repeatable process (deployment only, not a runtime participant). Multi-AZ redundancy targeting five nines availability. Evertz CloudBridge bookends the connection between AWS, New York and Atlanta. Future plans: live venue inputs on the ORT with switching between live and pre-recorded content, and muxing/compression in the cloud to hand off directly to an MVPD.

nodes.name: TWD/CNN Center (Atlanta on-prem)
nodes.notes: Techwood / CNN Center on-prem site in Atlanta. Linear Ops QCs the master files here. Receives the cloud playout as a unicast signal, compresses it and brings it to the uplink. An on-site auto changeover switch selects between Techwood playout, CNN Center playout and cloud playout. Evertz CloudBridge endpoint in Atlanta.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores all master files for all the brands. Files arrive via Aspera and are registered in Evertz Mediator.

nodes.name: EC2 (Evertz ORT playout)
nodes.notes: EC2 instances running Evertz ORT software; files are played out using Evertz Playtime. 10 channels per AZ in us-east-1 (30 channels total), each channel with a primary and a backup. Supported by Auto Scaling groups. Multi-AZ redundancy targeting five nines availability. Evertz CloudBridge carries the signal from the ORT back to site.

nodes.name: Direct Connect
nodes.notes: Carries the playout back to prem as a unicast signal. Evertz CloudBridge bookends the connection (AWS, New York, Atlanta). Also carries the BCP path to Hudson Yards in New York.

nodes.name: Uplink (ATL / NYC)
nodes.notes: Satellite uplinks for distribution to affiliates. The Atlanta uplink is fed from the on-prem site after compression; the NYC (Hudson Yards) uplink is fed by the BCP path with 8 channels.

edges.notes: Master files QC'd by Linear Ops in Atlanta are sent via Aspera up to S3.
Once registered in Evertz Mediator, the files are transferred to the local EC2 running Evertz ORT.
Playout from Evertz Playtime goes out via Direct Connect, using Evertz CloudBridge.
Playout returns to prem as a unicast signal: the 'X chain', a tertiary path to air.
The signal is compressed and brought to the uplink for distribution to affiliates.
BCP path: Direct Connect to Hudson Yards (NYC), 8 channels, also fed to an uplink. Stated in the audio; not in the connection ledger.
